before.summary: Leashed pets may visit the Convoy Point grounds and Elliott Key, but not Boca Chita Key.

after.summary: Leashed pets may visit the Convoy Point grounds and developed areas on Elliott Key, but not Boca Chita Key.

why: Pets are limited to the Convoy Point grounds and Elliott Key developed areas only; no trail is open to them, so roads, not trails.

before.summary: Leashed pets may use roads and paved areas, and some paved trails at Wetherill Mesa, but not trails or sites.

after.summary: Leashed pets may use roads and paved areas on Mesa Top Loop and Park Point, and Wetherill Mesa trails except Step House and Long House.

why: Rule said pets are banned from all trails, but the page allows every Wetherill Mesa trail except Step House and Long House; rules and summary corrected.

before.summary: Only a few listed trails, roads and paved trails allow leashed dogs.

after.summary: Leashed dogs may use roads and a few paved trails such as Desert Ecology and Desert Discovery; all other trails are closed to them.

why: Card lacked the trail ban and the named dog-friendly trails; added from the pets page.

before.summary: Leashed pets may use a few trails and plowed roads, but not Cleetwood Cove Trail or the lake.

after.summary: Leashed pets may use a few trails and plowed roads, but not Cleetwood Cove Trail or the lake.

why: Added the list of the only trails open to pets, which the trails policy rests on.

before.summary: Leashed pets are allowed on roads such as Mauna Loa Road and in most parking areas, not in many other areas.

after.summary: Leashed pets are allowed on roads such as Mauna Loa Road and in most parking areas, not in many other areas.

why: Roads policy had no quoted trail ban; added the list of prohibited areas from the park release.

before.summary: Pets can go only where cars go: roads, parking lots and campgrounds, not on trails.

after.summary: Pets can go only where cars go: roads, parking lots and campgrounds, not on trails.

why: Roads policy rested only on a leash rule; added the quoted trail ban.

before.summary: Pets are banned from trails, overlooks and the backcountry; only paved roads, campgrounds and the Potash/Shafer drive.

after.summary: Pets are banned from trails, overlooks and the backcountry; only paved roads, campgrounds and the Potash/Shafer drive.

why: Roads policy rested only on a leash rule; added the compendium trail ban.

before.summary: Leashed pets may use the Lexington Arch Trail and the Baker to visitor center trail only.

after.summary: Leashed pets may use the Lexington Arch Trail and the Baker to visitor center trail only.

why: Added the quoted trail ban behind the trails policy.

before.summary: Leashed dogs may use trails such as those around Artist Point.

after.summary: Leashed dogs may use trails such as the Pacific Crest Trail at Snoqualmie Pass.

why: Card was about Artist Point and Table Mountain, which are in the Mt. Baker unit; replaced with Snoqualmie pages.

before.summary: Dogs may use most trails; banned in the Enchantments.

after.summary: Dogs are allowed on most wilderness trails, under control.

why: Card was about the Enchantments and Alpine Lakes Wilderness, which are in the Wenatchee unit; replaced with forest-wide rules.

before.summary: Pets stay near roads; only the Roadside Hiking Trail and Roadside Bike Trail allow leashed pets.

after.summary: Leashed pets may walk the Roadside Hiking Trail and Roadside Bike Trail, plus roads, parking lots and campgrounds.

why: The pets page opens the Roadside Hiking Trail and Roadside Bike Trail to leashed pets, so trails, not roads.

before.summary: Pets may walk roads, the campground, picnic area, orchards and parking lots, not most trails.

after.summary: Leashed pets may walk the Fremont River Trail to Hattie's Field, plus roads, the campground, orchards and parking lots.

why: The pets page opens part of the Fremont River Trail to leashed pets, so trails, not roads.

before.summary: Pets are permitted in developed campgrounds, on beaches, in picnic areas and on roads, not on trails.

after.summary: Leashed pets may visit Freshwater, Gold Bluffs and Crescent beaches, campgrounds, picnic areas and roads, but no trails.

why: The pets page opens three named beaches to leashed pets, and a beach counts as trails, not roads.

before.summary: Pets are allowed only on paved surfaces, including a half mile of the Rim Trail and the Shared-use Path.

after.summary: Pets may go only on paved surfaces: roads, campgrounds, viewpoints, the Shared-use Path and the paved Rim Trail by the lodge.

why: Pets are limited to paved paths in developed areas (the Shared-use Path and the paved Rim Trail between Sunset and Sunrise Points), which don't count as trails, so roads.
